Title: [ARCH-01] Define endpoint role and resource authorization matrix
Body: Create a versioned matrix covering every API route, allowed role, patient ownership rule, audit requirement, and anonymous exception. Review it with clinical, billing, and operations stakeholders. Acceptance criteria: every controller action is listed exactly once; anonymous access is limited to login and invitation completion; patient-owned versus staff-wide access is explicit; the matrix is checked into the repository and linked from authorization tests.

Title: [ARCH-02] Introduce named authorization policies and current-user access
Body: Replace per-controller Authorization-header parsing and TokenRoleValidator calls with ASP.NET Core named policies, role claims, and a current-user abstraction. Add resource authorization for patient ownership. Depends on ARCH-01. Acceptance criteria: controllers use named policies; no controller manually parses bearer tokens; cross-patient access returns the approved 403/404; policy and API integration tests cover every role.

Title: [ARCH-03] Add application use-case layer
Body: Create an Application boundary for SearchPatients, CompleteEncounter, PostPayment, and GenerateInvitation. Move orchestration, transaction boundaries, and access decisions out of controllers. Depends on ARCH-01 and ARCH-02. Acceptance criteria: controllers bind/validate, call a use case, and map results; use cases do not depend on MVC or HTTP headers; one patient and one billing flow are migrated with tests.

Title: [ARCH-04] Separate infrastructure persistence from domain and application code
Body: Move EF Core, repositories, password storage, invitation persistence, and external adapters behind Infrastructure interfaces. Keep Domain free of EF, JWT, HTTP, and configuration dependencies. Depends on ARCH-03. Acceptance criteria: Domain has no EF or ASP.NET references; Application depends on ports; wiring is centralized; tests use a test persistence adapter.

Title: [ARCH-05] Standardize API contracts with DTOs and ProblemDetails
Body: Define request/response DTOs per feature, remove EF entity serialization, and configure RFC 7807 ProblemDetails with validation and correlation IDs. Depends on ARCH-03. Acceptance criteria: no API action returns a persistence entity; credentials and internal graph details are excluded; validation/not-found/forbidden/unexpected errors have stable shapes; representative contract tests exist.

Title: [ARCH-06] Add audit logging for sensitive operations
Body: Implement append-only audit events for PHI reads/exports, credential changes, invitation generation/use, and billing mutations. Record actor, action, resource, timestamp, correlation ID, and outcome without secrets or unnecessary PHI. Depends on ARCH-02 and ARCH-03. Acceptance criteria: required operations emit events; failed operations are recorded safely; retention and access are documented.

Title: [ARCH-07] Optimize patient and invoice query boundaries
Body: Add indexed search/filter fields, bounded pagination, cancellation tokens, and projection-based queries. Replace invoice N+1 loading with batched projections and add optimistic concurrency. Depends on ARCH-03 and ARCH-05. Acceptance criteria: patient/invoice endpoints return bounded pages; query count does not grow linearly; indexes are verified; concurrent updates return a controlled conflict.

Title: [ARCH-08] Split Angular into feature data-access boundaries
Body: Organize Angular code by auth, patients, scheduling, encounters, billing, and reports. Keep shared HTTP/auth state in core and use typed API models. Depends on ARCH-05. Acceptance criteria: feature internals are not cross-imported; API/auth behavior is centralized; routes and navigation use shared role definitions; patients and billing are migrated without regressions.

Title: [ARCH-09] Decide and document the identity/session strategy
Body: Evaluate ASP.NET Core Identity versus a hosted provider and cookie sessions versus bearer tokens. Compare MFA, lockout, reset, refresh rotation, ownership, cost, and regulatory requirements. Record an ADR and migration plan. Depends on ARCH-01. Acceptance criteria: selected and rejected options are documented; session behavior and CSRF are specified; migration and rollback are identified; security review signs off.

Title: [ARCH-10] Define background jobs and integration ports
Body: Create ports and operational contracts for reminders, reports, pharmacy/laboratory integrations, and payment/insurance integrations. Select durable jobs, retry/dead-letter policy, idempotency, and observability. Depends on ARCH-03 and ARCH-04. Acceptance criteria: retryable work is not inside HTTP requests; jobs have idempotency/retry behavior; failures are visible; one workflow uses the boundary.

Title: [ARCH-11] Establish observability and operational readiness
Body: Add structured logging, correlation propagation, dependency health checks, latency/error/auth metrics, and alerts. Depends on ARCH-03 and ARCH-06. Acceptance criteria: requests trace across API/database/jobs/audit; liveness and readiness are distinct; critical alerts exist; logs redact tokens, passwords, and sensitive patient content.

Title: [ARCH-12] Define production data protection and recovery runbook
Body: Document SQL backups, encryption, restore testing, migration rollout/rollback, retention, data residency, and recovery objectives. Execute a non-production restore rehearsal. Depends on ARCH-04 and ARCH-06. Acceptance criteria: RPO/RTO are approved; another operator can execute the runbook; migration rollback is tested; restore evidence is attached to a release record.

Title: [P0] Enforce default-deny authorization for PHI and billing endpoints
Body: Protect PatientsController, InvoicesController, DashboardController, and every clinical/billing route. Define named role/resource policies, remove duplicated token parsing, and add 401/403 plus cross-patient IDOR tests. Acceptance: anonymous protected calls return 401, wrong roles return 403, patient ownership is enforced, and only login/invitation completion are anonymous.

Title: [P0] Remove secrets and development URLs from production configuration
Body: Move JWT/database/frontend settings to environment or a secret manager, validate them at startup, enforce HTTPS/HSTS, configure production CORS, and route Angular services through environment.apiUrl. Acceptance: no secret, LocalDB, localhost URL, or placeholder production host is required in a production build.

Title: [P0] Stop exposing credentials and upgrade password hashing
Body: Return user DTOs that exclude Password, replace unsalted SHA-256 with PasswordHasher/PBKDF2/Argon2id, remove known seed credentials, and document reset/migration. Acceptance: hashes never appear in JSON, new passwords are salted/slow-hashed, and serialization tests pass.

Title: [P0] Restore real frontend authentication and centralized 401 handling
Body: Make authGuard reject missing/expired tokens, return UrlTree redirects, add an HTTP interceptor for auth and 401 logout, centralize API URLs, and document or replace localStorage token storage. Acceptance: guarded routes and API calls behave correctly for anonymous, expired, and valid sessions.

Title: [P1] Make invitation links durable, single-use, and rate-limited
Body: Replace IMemoryCache invitation state with a durable hashed token record containing expiry, used-at, patient ID, and attempt metadata. Consume atomically and rate-limit invalid attempts. Acceptance: links survive restart/scale-out, replay returns 401, and invalid links reveal no patient data.

Title: [P1] Add safe error handling, async correctness, and input limits
Body: Add centralized ProblemDetails handling and correlation IDs, remove .Result/.Wait() from request handlers, return generic client errors, validate bounds, and paginate unbounded patient/invoice/report queries. Acceptance: no exception details leak and response sizes are bounded.

Title: [P1] Establish a production verification pipeline
Body: Fix authentication fixtures missing User.Role, add authorization/DTO/security regression tests and Angular guard/interceptor tests, then define CI restore/build/test steps. Acceptance: dotnet test, npm ci, npm test, and npm run build pass from their project directories and block merges on failure.

Title: [P1] Remove misleading login and navigation affordances
Body: Remove or implement noopClick login/social actions, replace # routes, and make navigation role-aware. Add keyboard/focus and responsive checks. Acceptance: every visible action works or clearly reports unavailable, no # navigation remains, and mobile login/sidebar workflows are usable.

Title: [UX-01] Define the MVP workflows and remove out-of-scope promises
Body: Create a one-page workflow map for receptionist, doctor, billing, and patient registration. Mark each current route/control as keep, redesign, hide, or remove. The MVP should focus on sign-in, dashboard, patient search/profile, scheduling, encounters, prescriptions, billing, and logout. Acceptance: every visible feature has an owner and supported workflow; unsupported social login, self-signup, and placeholder modules are removed from the UI; the workflow map is checked into the repository.

Title: [UX-02] Replace the flat sidebar with role-based MVP navigation
Body: Reduce the sidebar to grouped workflows: Today, Patients, Clinical, Billing, Reports, and Administration. Render only routes allowed by the authenticated user's role and remove duplicate/history clutter from the primary navigation. Acceptance: receptionist, doctor, billing, and admin each see a short relevant menu; active route is obvious; no unauthorized item is displayed; no navigation target is '#'.

Title: [UX-03] Remove dead and misleading login actions
Body: Remove noopClick links and unsupported Google/Facebook/Apple actions, or implement them fully. Remove role preset buttons unless they represent a supported non-production demo mode. Keep one clear sign-in path with username, password, password visibility, submit, and honest recovery guidance. Acceptance: every visible control has a real outcome; no preventDefault-only action remains; login works by keyboard and screen reader.

Title: [UX-04] Rebuild login around clear states and safe feedback
Body: Replace alert() and console response logging with an inline status region and field-level validation. Add loading, invalid credentials, network failure, locked/inactive account, and success states while preserving focus and preventing duplicate submissions. Acceptance: errors are understandable and accessible; sensitive response data is not logged; the user always knows whether submission is in progress or complete.

Title: [UX-05] Establish shared loading, empty, error, and success patterns
Body: Create reusable Angular patterns for page loading, empty results, failed requests, saved changes, destructive confirmation, and session expiry. Apply them first to patient search/profile and billing. Acceptance: those workflows do not use browser alerts for normal product feedback; every async view has loading/empty/error states; status messages are announced accessibly; retry actions are available where appropriate.

Title: [UX-06] Make the patient workflow the primary operational path
Body: Design the receptionist flow as: search patient, review identity, open record, perform the next allowed action, and return to context. Add clear search, no-results, duplicate-risk, unsaved-change, and save-success states. Acceptance: a receptionist can reach a patient encounter in two predictable steps after search; patient identity remains visible on detail/edit views; destructive actions require confirmation.

Title: [UX-07] Simplify clinical and billing screens for decision-making
Body: Audit encounters, prescriptions, billing, and reports to remove decorative panels and low-value fields from the primary view. Surface status, owner, date, next action, and validation errors first; move history and secondary details behind deliberate navigation. Acceptance: a doctor can identify the next clinical action without scanning unrelated modules; billing users can distinguish pending, overdue, paid, and failed states without color alone.

Title: [UX-08] Make the application responsive and keyboard accessible
Body: Test login, sidebar, patient search, patient detail, encounter, and billing at 320px, 768px, and desktop widths. Fix overflow, focus order, focus visibility, labels, live regions, touch targets, and table behavior. Acceptance: primary workflows complete without horizontal page scrolling; all actions are keyboard reachable; focus is visible; status/error text is linked to its control.

Title: [UX-09] Add a role-based UX acceptance test pass
Body: Create a lightweight test matrix for receptionist, doctor, billing, admin, anonymous, expired-session, and unauthorized scenarios. Verify visible navigation, route redirects, primary workflows, and error states against the authorization matrix. Acceptance: the test matrix is versioned; critical role journeys are automated or documented as repeatable checks; UI never presents a workflow the API will reject without explanation.
